Board can give up area, but not much. Routability stays ≥0.95 down to about 1197 mm², so I'm cutting from 1250 to 1205. That keeps a small margin and frees about 101 mm³ (45 × 2.24). It is only ~8% of the 1246 mm³ overage, so the other leads need to find ~1145 mm³ more.

I can't go below ~1200 mm² without breaking the 10-layer routing on the W1000. The siren is the safety-critical feature, so I'd protect battery energy and the siren's acoustic volume first. Antenna, NFC, haptics, and structure should look for the larger cuts. I'm probing 1197, 1200, and 1215 to confirm the routability floor.

Battery is at 3786 mm³ and 59.78 h, right at the ~60 h target. Siren endurance scales with cell energy, so I can't give volume until acoustics tells us the siren power margin. Battery is also 34% of the interior, so cutting it wouldn't fix an overage of 1145 mm³ on its own.

Battery has two constraints. Thickness must stay at or below 4.8 mm, so A_batt must be at least 789 mm² at this volume. The caseback also caps A_batt at roughly 823 mm² alongside the thermal spreader.

I'm probing small volume cuts to measure runtime sensitivity. The biggest cuts have to come from antenna (1500), structure (1800), and acoustics (1460), which should justify those volumes against the 86 dB target. I OBJECT while the interior is over by 1145 mm³.

Antenna can give volume, but I don't yet know how much L5 efficiency it costs. L5 is 0.208 at 1500 mm³ and a 1.2 mm wall. I'm moving my claim to 1300 mm³ (-200) as a good-faith cut. My probes will show whether the efficiency curve is flat enough to go lower.

Wall thickness is the cheapest lever. Each -0.1 mm returns 150 mm³ to the pool and reduces detuning, so it helps antenna efficiency. Structure should say what a 1.1 mm wall costs in drop and strength margin.

Perimeter use is 1820 of 2400 mm³, so that pool isn't the constraint. The interior total is. Acoustics and structure, please justify your volumes against 86 dB and the wall minimum.

I OBJECT while the interior is over.

Thermal is at 320 mm² (250 mm³) and skin temperature is exactly 43.0 C, so I have no margin and can't give area at a 1.2 mm wall. Cutting area pushes skin temperature over the limit. The spreader is only 250 mm³ of the 945 mm³ overage. The big cuts have to come from antenna, structure, and acoustics, and from wall thickness.

I'm probing what a 1.1 mm wall does to skin temperature. If a thinner wall costs me temperature, I can offset it with a few more mm² of spreader. At 0.78 mm per mm², that costs far less than the 150 mm³ the thinner wall returns to the pool. Structure should report the drop and strength margin at 1.1 mm.

I OBJECT while the interior is over.

Structure can't give volume yet. At a 1.2 mm wall, 9.0 mm² port and 1800 mm³ ribs, my pressure margin is 1.438 against the 1.5 requirement, so I'm failing my own requirement. A 1.1 mm wall would make that worse, so I can't offer it as a cut.

Ribs, wall and port are the three levers. I'm probing each one:
- Ribs at 2100 mm³ (+300 mm³).
- Port at 7 mm² (acoustics, what-if only).
- Wall at 1.3 mm (+150 mm³ cost to everyone).

I'll report the margin per mm³ so we can pick the cheapest fix. Acoustics, please say what a smaller port does to 86 dB.

I OBJECT.

Acoustics fails its own requirement. The siren needs 9.08 W against the 1.0 W cap, so endurance is only 0.34 h. The resonance is at 5.6 kHz, and the siren is the safety-critical feature. I can't give volume until I find a tuning that gets the siren under 1 W, because size alone won't fix a 9x power gap.

Mesh resistance, outlet length and the back-cavity split are free of the shared pools, so I'm using them first. I'm dropping the mesh to the 20 rayl floor and lengthening the outlet to lower the resonance. I'm also probing a smaller port, 7 mm², which would help Structure's pressure margin, and a smaller volume. I'll report the siren power and SII for each.

Haptics can give volume. The LRA force is 1.069 N at 350 mm³, and my minimum for 0.9 N is about 295 mm³. I'm cutting to 310 mm³, which keeps roughly 0.95 N and about 5% margin. That returns 40 mm³ to the pool, so the haptics cut is small. Probes at 295, 300 and 305 mm³ will confirm the force floor.

The overage is still about 905 mm³ after my cut. Most of it has to come from structure ribs, acoustics volume, antenna and the wall, not from haptics.

The siren is the safety-critical feature, so Acoustics should say what siren power margin it needs. If Acoustics finds a tuning that fixes the power gap, it can then trade volume. Structure's pressure fix, whether a smaller port or more ribs, also needs to be costed against the pool.

I OBJECT because the interior is still over, even though my own requirement is met.

NFC can give volume. My read range is 18.2 mm against a 10 mm requirement, so I have about 8 mm of margin. I'm cutting from 500 to 390 mm³ (loop 320 to 250, ferrite 180 to 140), which returns 110 mm³. I'm not claiming the minimum yet because I haven't measured the range there.

My probes cover the 290 mm³ floor (180/110) and two intermediate points. If the range stays comfortably above 10 mm, I'll cut further next round, possibly to about 290-340 mm³.

NFC is small, so the large cuts still have to come from structure, acoustics, antenna and the wall. Acoustics, please report siren power after retuning so the others know how much volume you actually need.

I OBJECT because the interior is still over, even though my own requirement is met.

Board is moving from 1205 to 1200 mm². Last round's probe showed routability of 0.952 at 1200 and 0.950 at 1197, so 1200 keeps a small margin above the 0.95 floor. That frees about 11 mm³ and puts board at 2688 mm³. I won't go below that: 1197 is exactly at the limit, with no room for layout changes.

Board has now given up about 112 mm³ in total. The ledger is still about 784 mm³ over, so I can't accept yet. The remaining cuts have to come from:
- Acoustics: siren retune results.
- Structure: the cheapest pressure-margin fix, a smaller port versus more ribs.
- Antenna: its L5 curve.
- NFC: a further cut toward its floor.

Board can't offset any of these. I'm probing 1198, 1199 and 1202 to map the margin.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³. The 3700 and 3600 mm³ probes put runtime sensitivity at about 0.0158 h/mm³, so each 100 mm³ costs about 1.6 h. Cutting 100 mm³ would drop runtime to about 58.2 h. Runtime does not depend on A_batt: 800 and 820 mm² gave the same 59.78 h. More area only thins the cell, to 4.62 mm at 820 mm².

The siren needs cell energy, so I can't cut until Acoustics reports its power after retuning. That is currently 9.08 W against the 1.0 W cap.

Caseback has 23 mm² slack (1120 of 1143). Thermal can take a few mm² from it for a 1.1 mm wall. I'm keeping 800 mm² so it stays available.

The biggest levers are structure ribs, acoustics volume, antenna, and wall thickness. I OBJECT while the interior is 784 mm³ over.

Antenna holds at 1300 mm³ this round. I've already given up 200 mm³ and it cost 0.052 of L5 efficiency (0.208 to 0.156).

The L5 curve at a 1.2 mm wall is steep and roughly linear:
- 1100 mm³: 0.112
- 1300 mm³: 0.156
- 1500 mm³: 0.208

Each 100 mm³ costs about 0.022 of efficiency, so I can't take another big cut without wrecking L5. A 1.1 mm wall adds only about +0.007, so it's not worth a strength hit that Structure can't afford.

The remaining 784 mm³ has to come from the larger blocks. Acoustics must retune the siren before it claims volume, and Structure must pick the cheapest fix for its pressure margin. I'm probing 1200 mm³, 1250 mm³, and 1300 mm³ at a 1.3 mm wall, to see how much a thicker wall costs L5.

I OBJECT while the interior is over.

Thermal's own requirement is met at 320 mm² (250 mm³), with skin temperature at 43.0 C and no margin to spare.

Last round's probes show wall thickness barely moves skin temperature:
- At a 1.1 mm wall, 320 mm² gives 42.99 C.
- At a 1.1 mm wall, 340 mm² gives 42.77 C.
- At a 1.3 mm wall, 300 mm² gives 43.25 C, which fails.

Sensitivity is about 0.011 C per mm², so a 1.1 mm wall costs Thermal nothing. If Structure can recover its pressure margin with a thinner wall, I won't block it. A 1.0 mm wall is also worth checking, and I'm probing it this round. I can't give area at 1.2 mm, and the spreader is only 250 of the 784 mm³ overage. I OBJECT while the interior is over.

Structure's pressure margin is 1.438 against the 1.5 requirement, so I OBJECT. The probes give three fixes:

| Fix | Margin change | Cost to the pool |
|---|---|---|
| Port 9 → 7 mm² | +0.124 (about 0.062 per mm²) | 0 mm³ |
| Wall +0.1 mm | +0.197 | 150 mm³ to everyone |
| Ribs +300 mm³ | +0.025 | 300 mm³ |

The port is the cheapest fix, and ribs are the weakest lever, at about 0.00008 per mm³. With the port at 7 mm², margin is 1.562. That leaves 0.06 to spend on ribs, so I could cut ribs by roughly 400 mm³ and still pass.

**Ask to Acoustics:** hold the port at 7 mm² or less, and tell me what it does to the siren and SII. Once the port is at 7, I'

Acoustics still fails: the siren needs 7.67 W against the 1.0 W cap, and endurance is 0.4 h. Split is the strongest free lever. Last round, split 0.78 → 0.60 cut the power from 7.4 to 2.2 W and moved resonance from 5.2 to 3.9 kHz. I'm going lower.

Structure, I accept port 7 mm² as a ceiling. The port-7 probe at 1200 mm³ was run at the old split, so it says little about the new tuning. The SII cost looks small, 88 → 86.6.

I'm claiming port 7 and split 0.5 now, and I won't give volume until the siren passes. The probes cover splits 0.5, 0.4 and 0.45, with longer outlets and a smaller volume.

Haptics is moving from 310 to 300 mm³, which returns another 10 mm³. Last round's probes gave 0.916 N at 300 mm³ (1.8% margin over 0.9 N) and 0.901 N at 295 mm³. 295 is the true floor, with only 0.001 N of margin, so I won't claim it. I'm probing 296 to 298 mm³ to see whether any margin is available between them.

Haptics has now given 50 mm³ in total, which is tiny against the 774 mm³ overage. The real levers are still elsewhere:
- **Structure:** the port-7 fix opens about 0.06 of pressure margin, which could pay for roughly 400 mm³ of ribs.
- **Acoustics:** it needs to pass the siren at 1.0 W before it can release volume.
- **Antenna and NFC:** each should give what its curve allows.

I OBJECT while the interior is over.

NFC is cutting to its floor: loop 180 mm³ and ferrite 110 mm³, 290 mm³ total. That returns 100 mm³ to the pool.

Last round's 180/110 probe gave 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement, a 2.7 mm margin (27%). That is enough, and I'm not holding back a reserve. NFC has now given 210 mm³ in total, 54% of its original 500.

After this cut the interior is still about 674 mm³ over. NFC has nothing left to give, since both variables are at their lower bounds. The remaining cuts have to come from:
- **Structure:** with the port at 7 mm², it can trade about 400 mm³ of ribs for pressure margin.
- **Acoustics:** it must pass the siren at 1.0 W before it can release volume.
- **Antenna and battery:** these are the remaining levers.

I OBJECT while the interior is over. My probes check the margin around the new claim.

Board holds at 1200 mm² (2688 mm³), with routability 0.952 against the 0.95 floor. Last round's probes gave 0.951 at 1198 and 0.952 at 1199. The step from 1200 to 1198 saves only about 4.5 mm³ and leaves 0.001 of margin, so it is not worth taking now. If the ledger ends up within about 5 mm³ of balancing, I'll take 1198 to close it.

Board has given up about 117 mm³ of its original claim. The remaining 674 mm³ overage has to come from the larger blocks:
- **Acoustics:** the siren must pass at 1.0 W so its 1460 mm³ can shrink.
- **Structure:** with the port at 7 mm², ribs can drop by about 400 mm³.
- **Battery and antenna:** each should give what its curve allows.

I OBJECT while the interior is over. This round I'm probing 1197, 1196 and 1195 to confirm where the floor is.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 800 mm². Runtime is 59.78 h, already just under the ~60 h target. Each 100 mm³ costs about 1.6 h.

The siren is the safety-critical feature, and its endurance depends on cell energy. Acoustics is still at 7.67 W and 0.4 h, so I can't cut energy until the siren is proven.

Once Acoustics shows a passing power figure with real endurance margin, I'll give back volume. I expect 100-200 mm³, which would put runtime at roughly 55-58 h. That is a marketing trade, and the siren outranks it.

Structure and Acoustics carry the large cuts. Structure can take about 400 mm³ from ribs once the port is at 7 mm². Acoustics must report a retuned siren power.

I'm probing 3700, 3650 and 3600 mm³ at 800 mm² to map the trade. I OBJECT while the interior is over.

Antenna holds at 1300 mm³, with L5 at 0.156. The L5 curve is linear at about 0.022 per 100 mm³, so I can't make a big cut. I've already given up 200 mm³ and 0.052 of efficiency.

The 1.3 mm wall probe shows a thicker wall costs 0.006 of L5. I'm opposed to any wall increase.

I'll release a final 50 mm³ (1250, L5 0.145) if that closes the ledger. That only makes sense once Structure's ribs, which can drop about 400 mm³ at port 7, and Acoustics' volume land. The 674 mm³ overage can't be closed by the small blocks.

Probes this round: 1250 and 1300 at a 1.1 mm wall, and 1280 at 1.2 mm.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³), with skin temperature at 43.00 C and no margin at a 1.2 mm wall.

- **Wall thickness:** it barely affects Thermal. At 320 mm², a 1.1 mm wall gives 42.99 C and a 1.0 mm wall gives 42.97 C. I won't block a thinner wall. Each 0.1 mm of wall returns 150 mm³ to everyone, which is far more than any other small cut offers.
- **Spreader area:** area is worth only about 0.011 C per mm². At a 1.0 mm wall I could trim to about 317 mm², which saves roughly 2 mm³. That is negligible, so I'm not claiming it.
- **Caseback:** Thermal needs no extra caseback area.

The 674 mm³ overage has to come from Structure's ribs, Acoustics' volume once the siren passes, a thinner wall, and Battery and Antenna. I OBJECT while the interior is over. My probes check 317 mm² at 1.0 mm, 320 mm² at 1.1 mm, and 310 mm² at 1.0 mm.

Structure is claiming ribs 1400 mm³, the lower bound, which returns 400 mm³ to the pool. The overage drops from 674 to about 274 mm³.

- **Margin:** port 7 mm² gives 1.562. Ribs at about 0.00008 per mm³ cost roughly 0.033 for 400 mm³, so margin should be about 1.529, above the 1.5 floor. The first probe checks this.
- **Wall:** the wall stays at 1.2 mm. A 1.1 mm wall loses 0.197 of margin, which ribs cannot recover.
- **Port:** Acoustics, the port must stay at 7 mm² or less, and every mm² below 7 returns about 0.062 of margin. A port near 4 mm² might allow a 1.1 mm wall, but I doubt the siren survives that. The third probe tests it.

The remaining 274 mm³ has to come from Acoustics, Battery and Antenna. I OBJECT while the interior is over.

Acoustics still fails: siren power is 1.925 W against the 1.0 W cap, and endurance is 1.49 h. Shrinking volume helps, which is the opposite of what I assumed. At 1300 mm³ power drops to 1.56 W and resonance rises to 3.49 kHz, while SII costs only about 1 point (82.3). I'm releasing 160 mm³ now, claiming V=1300, which cuts the overage to about 114 mm³.

Endurance is roughly 2.85 W·h divided by siren power. Three hours therefore needs about 0.93 W or less, and Battery must not cut cell energy below its current size. I'm probing 1100, 1000 and 1150 mm³ (with split 0.55) to find the power minimum. Port stays at 7 mm

Haptics moves from 300 to 297 mm³, which returns 3 mm³. Force at 297 is 0.907 N, a 0.7% margin over the 0.9 N floor. At 296 the margin is 0.4%, and at 295 it is 0.001 N. I'm not claiming those, because the evaluator is only probed in whole mm³ steps and I want some margin left on a safety-adjacent haptic alert.

After Acoustics' release the overage is about 114 mm³, and 3 mm³ from me barely changes it. The remaining cuts have to come from:
- **Acoustics:** a lower siren volume, if the 1100 and 1150 probes pass.
- **Antenna:** its offered 50 mm³.
- **Board:** the 1198 step, worth about 4.5 mm³, for the last few mm³.
- **Wall:** a thinner wall returns 150 mm³, but Structure says it can't recover the pressure margin.

I won't block any of these. I OBJECT while the interior is over.

NFC is already at both floors, with loop at 180 mm³ and ferrite at 110 mm³, so I have nothing more to give. Read range is 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement. Last round's probes show it is not very sensitive to either variable: ferrite +20 mm³ gives +0.3 mm, and loop +10 mm³ gives +0.3 mm. NFC has returned 210 mm³ of its original 500.

By my count the interior is still about 111 mm³ over once Acoustics' 1300 mm³ release lands. The ledger above still shows 1460 for acoustics. The remaining cuts have to come from these levers:
- **Acoustics:** the 1100 and 1150 mm³ probes, if the siren passes at 1.0 W.
- **Antenna:** its offered 50 mm³.
- **Board:** the 1198 step.
- **Battery:** volume only after the siren is proven, because endurance depends on cell energy.

The perimeter keepout is fine at 1480 of 2400 mm³. I'm OBJECTing only because the interior is over.

Board moves from 1200 to 1198 mm², which is 2683.5 mm³ and returns about 4.5 mm³. Routability is 0.951 against the 0.95 floor, so my own requirement is met.

Last round's probe at 1197 mm² gave exactly 0.950, which passes, but at 1196 it fails. 1197 is my hard floor and I'm holding it as a last-resort reserve. It is worth another 2 mm³ only if the ledger ends within that of balancing.

After Acoustics' 1300 mm³ release the overage is about 111 mm³. Board cannot close that. It has to come from:
- Acoustics, if the lower-volume probes show a lower siren power.
- Antenna's offered 50 mm³.
- Battery, once the siren is proven.
- A thinner wall, if Structure and Acoustics can find a combination with enough margin.

I OBJECT only because the interior is still over.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 800 mm². I will not cut cell energy until the siren is proven. Acoustics still shows 1.56-1.93 W and 0.4-1.5 h of endurance. Endurance is about 2.85 Wh divided by siren power, so a 3 h siren needs ≤0.93 W. Cutting 100 mm³ of cell would raise that requirement.

Battery cannot fix the siren by adding volume. Reaching 3 h at 1.56 W would take about 4.7 Wh, far more than the interior allows. The fix has to come from siren power. Acoustics, please report the real power minimum from your 1000-1150 mm³ probes.

Once a passing power is shown, I'll release 100-200 mm³ as a marketing trade. This round I'm probing a larger footprint (up to the 23 mm² of free caseback) to see whether it recovers runtime per mm³. I OBJECT while the interior is over.

Antenna releases the 50 mm³ I offered and moves to 1250 mm³. L5 should be about 0.145 at the 1.2 mm wall, which is the slope from my probes (0.152 at 1280, 0.156 at 1300). That is already 0.052 below my original efficiency. I will not go lower without evidence that it buys the siren something.

Acoustics' 1300 mm³ release isn't in the ledger yet. With it and my 50 mm³, the overage is about 56 mm³. Board's 1198 step (4.5 mm³) and Haptics' 3 mm³ are already counted, so the rest has to come from:
- **Acoustics:** its 1000–1150 mm³ probes.
- **Battery:** its 100–200 mm³ once the siren is proven.

I still oppose a thicker wall. I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³). Skin temperature is 43.00 °C at the 1.2 mm wall, so my requirement is met, with no margin.

- **Correction:** last round's 317 mm² at a 1.0 mm wall gave 43.01 °C and failed. I'm withdrawing my earlier offer to trim area. A 310 mm² spreader would give 43.09 °C. Trimming saves about 2 mm³ at most, so it isn't worth chasing.
- **Wall:** a thinner wall is fine with me. At 320 mm², 1.1 mm gives 42.99 °C and 1.0 mm gives 42.97 °C. Each 0.1 mm of wall returns 150 mm³, far more than any small cut can.
- **Caseback:** I need no extra area.

The overage is about 56 mm³ once Acoustics' release lands. It has to come from Acoustics' volume and Battery. I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Structure holds at ribs 1400 mm³ and wall 1.2 mm. Pressure margin is 1.529 against the 1.5 floor, so my requirement is met. I OBJECT only because the interior is still over.

The remaining overage is about 56 mm³ once Acoustics' 1300 mm³ release lands. Battery's cut would depend on a siren that isn't proven yet.

**Wall option:** a 1.1 mm wall returns 150 mm³, which closes the ledger outright. Last round's probe at 1.1 mm wall and port 4 mm² gave margin 1.527, which passes. At port 7 the 1.1 mm wall fails (about 1.33), and margin falls about 0.065 per mm² of port. The port ceiling at 1.1 mm is therefore about 4.4 mm².

**Request to Acoustics:** report siren power and endurance at port 4.2 to 4.5 mm² and V=1100 to 1300 mm³. If the siren holds at 1.0 W with a smaller port, I'll move to a 1.1 mm wall. If it doesn't, the wall stays at 1.2 mm.

My probes this round test the port ceiling at 1.

Acoustics claims V=1300 mm³ now. Last round's 1.56 W at that volume came from a probe, so it isn't in the ledger yet. That cuts the overage to about 56 mm³. My own requirement still fails: the siren is 1.56 W against the 1.0 W cap, and endurance is under 2 h. I OBJECT.

I'm not asking for a smaller port until I know what it does to siren power. A smaller port lowers resonance, and I expect that to hurt, since shrinking volume helped by raising it. Structure, I'll report the port 4.3 results next round.

Probes this round:
1. V=1100, port 7, split 0.55, h_out 3.0.
2. V=1200, port 4.3, h_out 0.3, which tests a shorter outlet to offset the smaller port.
3. V=1300, port 7, h_out 1.0.

Battery, hold your cell energy until the siren is proven.

Haptics holds at 297 mm³, with force at 0.907 N against the 0.9 N floor, so my requirement is met. I OBJECT only because the interior is still about 56 mm³ over.

- **Reserve:** the evaluator gave 0.904 N at 296 and 0.901 N at 295, and 294 fails at 0.898 N. My hard floor is 295, which would return 2 mm³. I'll take it only if the ledger ends within about 2 mm³ of balancing. Taking it now would trade away safety margin on the haptic alert for a negligible gain.
- **Where the 56 mm³ must come from:**
  - **Acoustics:** its 1100 mm³ probe, if siren power drops.
  - **Wall:** a 1.1 mm wall returns 150 mm³, if Structure and Acoustics find a viable port.
  - **Battery:** its 100-200 mm³ once the siren is proven.
- **Priority:** the siren outranks every small cut here. Nobody should shave volume that would hurt siren power or cell energy to save a few mm³.

NFC is already at both floors (loop 180, ferrite 110), so I have nothing more to give. Read range is 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement, so my own requirement is met.

The perimeter keepout is fine at 1430 of 2400 mm³. The interior is still about 56 mm³ over. I can't close that. It has to come from:
- **Acoustics:** a lower siren power at a smaller volume, which would also let Battery release cell volume.
- **Wall:** a 1.1 mm wall returns 150 mm³, if Structure and Acoustics find a port that works.
- **Battery:** its 100-200 mm³, once the siren is proven.

The siren outranks every small cut. I'm not offering anything that would hurt it. I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Board holds at 1198 mm² (2683.5 mm³), routability 0.951, so my own requirement is met. I OBJECT only because the interior is 56 mm³ over.

My 1197 floor (0.950, saves 2.2 mm³) is too small to matter, so I'm keeping the margin for now. If the ledger ends within 2 mm³ of balancing, I'll take it.

The siren is safety-critical, so I'm not asking Acoustics or Battery to cut anything that hurts it. The only cut large enough is the wall: each 0.1 mm returns 150 mm³ and covers the whole overage. Thermal has confirmed 1.1 mm is fine. Structure's limit is a port of about 4.4 mm² or less at 1.1 mm. Acoustics, please report siren power at port 4.0-4.4 mm² and V=1200-1300 mm³.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 800 mm². Runtime is 59.78 h, so my requirement is met. I OBJECT because the interior is 56 mm³ over.

- **Siren:** Endurance is about 2.85 Wh divided by siren power. A 3 h siren needs ≤0.93 W, and Acoustics is at 1.56 W. Cutting cell volume only makes that worse, so I'm not cutting until a passing power is shown.
- **Wall:** I support a 1.1 mm wall with a port ≤4.4 mm². It closes the ledger without touching the cell. Acoustics, please report siren power at port 4.0-4.4 mm² and V=1200-1300 mm³.
- **Probes:** I'm testing a larger footprint (up to 823 mm², the free caseback), which may recover runtime per mm³. This is what-if only, so Battery does not claim it yet.

Antenna holds at 1250 mm³, with L5 at 0.145 at the 1.2 mm wall. I support the 1.1 mm wall. My probe at 1250 mm³ and 1.1 mm gave L5 0.151, so a thinner wall improves L5 by about 0.006 at no volume cost to me. It also returns 150 mm³ and closes the 56 mm³ overage without touching the cell.

The condition is that Acoustics shows the siren works at a port of 4.4 mm² or less. The siren outranks my L5, and I won't hold volume against it. If a probe shows my volume buys siren endurance, I'll release more.

This round I'm probing the wall effect at several volumes. I OBJECT only because the interior is still 56 mm³ over.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³), 43.00 °C at the 1.2 mm wall, so my own requirement is met. I have nothing left to trim at the current wall.

- **Wall:** I support 1.1 mm. At 320 mm² it gives 42.99 °C, so I need no area change. At 1.0 mm it gives 42.97 °C.
- **Where the volume has to come from:** The 56 mm³ overage is too large for any small cut. A 1.1 mm wall returns 150 mm³ and closes it.
- **Gating item:** Acoustics must show the siren works at a port of 4.4 mm² or less. The siren outranks everything here.
- **Probes this round:** 320 mm² at 1.1 mm to confirm, and 315 and 310 mm² at 1.0 mm to see how much area a 1.0 mm wall could return.

I OBJECT only because the interior is still over.

Structure holds ribs at 1400 mm³ and the wall at 1.2 mm for now. Margin is 1.529, so my requirement is met. I OBJECT only because the interior is 56 mm³ over.

There is an option between 1.2 mm and 1.1 mm. Fitting my probes, margin rises about 0.2 per 0.1 mm of wall and falls about 0.065 per mm² of port. That gives these port ceilings:
- **1.15 mm wall:** port ≤ ~5.9 mm². It returns 75 mm³, which covers the 56 mm³ overage with ~19 mm³ spare.
- **1.1 mm wall:** port ≤ ~4.4 mm². It returns 150 mm³.

Extra ribs are not worth it. +100 mm³ buys only about 0.009 of margin.

Last round's results:
- **Outlet height:** a longer outlet helps. Going from h_out 1.0 to 3.0 at V=1300 cut power from 2.19 W to 1.56 W.
- **Short outlet:** the 0.3 mm outlet at port 4.3 was a clear failure at 4.93 W.
- **Resonance:** lower resonance appears to help. 4291 Hz gave 3.4 W and 3491 Hz gave 1.56 W.
